overview: White supports e4 with 2.d3 instead of developing the knight, a slow King's Indian Attack or reversed Philidor set-up. After 2...d5 White usually plays Nd2, Ngf3 and g3 or Be2, and Black has an easy game with the centre. Neither side takes risks early; White rarely gets an edge.

white_ideas.idea: Build the e4-d3 centre with Nd2, Ngf3, g3 and Bg2 and keep a flexible game.
Wait for Black to commit before striking with c4 or exd5.

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...d5 and ...e5, then develop naturally.
Equalise easily, using the extra tempo in a reversed Philidor.

typical_structures.structure: Philidor-like with colours reversed: White pawns e4-d3, Black d5-e5 centre.

character.notes: Slow, low-risk development; few ways to lose quickly. Solid.

soundness.notes: Sound but passive; Black equalises easily.

approach.notes: Rare at the top. 2.d3 is seldom chosen by strong players, though it is a respectable set-up. Offbeat with low confidence.

level.notes: Easy to play; no theory, but not a repertoire anyone relies on. Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Philidor transposition
sublines_that_differ.how: Reversed set-up leading to a Philidor-like game.

character.reason: Slow and passive with few early tactics.

structure.reason: Centre tension undecided for a long time.

level.reason: Simple to play but not a recommended first repertoire.

plans.reason: No plan is characteristic enough to name.
